title: In vitro drug metabolism study of montelukast metabolites using mass spectrometry
author: Marques, Pinheiro, et al.

steps.title: Prepare S9 homogenization buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1.21 g Tris‑HCl, 2.4 g KCl and 0.15 g EDTA in Milli‑Q water and bring the volume to 200 mL with water; adjust pH to 7.4 before adding KCl and EDTA, store the buffer at 4 °C (stable ≥6 months, watch for fungal particles).

steps.title: Euthanize animals and collect tissues
steps.instruction: Anesthetize each mouse with isoflurane, sacrifice by cervical dislocation, dissect the desired organs (e.g., liver, lung, kidney, brain) into micro‑tubes or conical centrifuge tubes, and immediately store the tissues in liquid nitrogen until homogenization.

steps.title: Homogenize tissues
steps.instruction: Place frozen tissue on ice, add 5–10 mL of ice‑cold S9 homogenization solution per gram of tissue, and homogenize with a Potter‑Elvehjem homogenizer or micro‑pestle until a uniform suspension is obtained.

steps.title: Centrifuge homogenate
steps.instruction: Spin the homogenates at 9,000 × g for 20 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Collect S9 fraction and quantify protein
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant (S9 fraction) to a fresh tube, determine its protein concentration with the Pierce™ Bicinchoninic Acid (BCA) assay according to the manufacturer’s protocol, and keep the fraction on ice (22–24 °C ambient temperature is acceptable for short periods).

steps.title: Aliquot and store S9 fractions
steps.instruction: Dispense the S9 fraction into small aliquots to avoid freeze‑thaw cycles; for example, 500 µL at 20 mg mL⁻¹ for up to 50 assays or 200 µL at 10 mg mL⁻¹ for up to 20 assays, then store at –80 °C until use.

steps.title: Prepare hepatocyte seeding environment
steps.instruction: Decontaminate the laminar flow cabinet surface with 70 % ethanol, ensure all tubes and pipettes are autoclaved, turn on the water bath to 37 °C, warm the hepatocyte culture medium, and fill a 50 mL conical tube with approximately 20 mL of the warmed medium.

steps.title: Incubate cells with drug
steps.instruction: Add the drug of interest to the cultured cells at a non‑toxic concentration (verify cell viability beforehand) and incubate for 0.5–2 h at 37 °C (or as required).

steps.title: Extract metabolites
steps.instruction: Extract drug metabolites from the cells using one of two protocols that depend on the cells’ adherence characteristics (details not provided in the source). No normalization to control samples is required for metabolite identification.

steps.title: Set up UHPLC conditions
steps.instruction: Install a Luna 3 µm C18(2) column (100 Å, 150 × 2 mm) on the Elute UHPLC, set column temperature to 35 °C, flow rate to 200 µL min⁻¹, and use the following gradient with mobile phase A (0.1 % formic acid in water for ESI⁺ or 5 mM ammonium acetate pH 6.5 for ESI⁻) and mobile phase B (0.1 % formic acid in acetonitrile): 0–4 min 5 % B; 4–22 min 5 %→100 % B; 24 min 100 % B; 24–25 min 100 %→5 % B; then a 10‑min re‑equilibration.

steps.title: Configure mass spectrometer
steps.instruction: Set the Impact II Q‑ToF parameters: capillary voltage 4.5 kV (ESI⁺) or 3 kV (ESI⁻); end‑plate offset 500 V; nebulizer 2.0 bar; dry gas (N₂) 8.0 L min⁻¹; dry heater 220 °C; transfer funnel 1/2 RF power 150/200 Vpp; hexapole RF power 50 Vpp; ion energy 4.0 eV; low‑mass cut‑off 50 m/z; collision energy 7.0 eV; collision RF power 650 Vpp; transfer time 80 µs; pre‑pulse storage 5 µs; absolute intensity threshold 25 counts per 1,000; MS/MS scan range 50–1500 m/z at 2.00 Hz; auto‑MS/MS trigger threshold 400 counts per 1,000, limit 3 precursors, exclude after 3 spectra; overall acquisition m/z range 50–1500 at 2 Hz.

steps.title: Convert raw data to mzXML
steps.instruction: Use ProteoWizard MSConvert to convert the instrument’s raw files to mzXML format.

steps.title: Mass detection in MZmine
steps.instruction: In MZmine v3, run the Mass Detection module with centroid detector; set noise level to 1,000 for positive‑ion mode and 50 for negative‑ion mode.

steps.title: Build chromatograms
steps.instruction: Run the ADAP Chromatogram Builder with: minimal group size = 2 scans; group intensity threshold = 50; minimal highest intensity = 50; scan‑to‑scan m/z tolerance = 3 mDa.

steps.title: Smooth chromatograms
steps.instruction: Apply the Savitzky‑Golay smoothing algorithm with a retention‑time smoothing window of 5.

steps.title: Resolve local minima
steps.instruction: Use the Local Minimum Feature Resolver with: retention‑time tolerance = 0.15 min; MS¹‑MS² precursor tolerance = 3 mDa; limit by RT edges = yes; dimension = retention time; chromatographic threshold = 90.0 %; minimum search‑range RT = 0.05 min; minimum relative height = 0.0 %; minimum absolute height = 1,000; peak‑top/edge ratio = 1.80; minimum data points = 4.5.

steps.title: Apply isotope filtering
steps.instruction: First run the 13C isotope filter (isotope grouper) with m/z tolerance = 5 mDa, RT tolerance = 0.05 min, monotonic shape = yes, maximum charge = 1, representative isotope = lowest m/z; then (optionally) run the Isotope Peak Finder with appropriate chemical elements, m/z tolerance = 1.5 mDa, maximum charge = 1.6.

steps.title: Align peaks across samples
steps.instruction: Execute the Join Aligner with m/z tolerance = 5 mDa, RT tolerance = 0.1 min, weight for m/z = 3, weight for RT = 1 (adjust RT tolerance to 0.2 min if peak drift is observed).

steps.title: Annotate peaks with custom database
steps.instruction: Create a CSV database containing columns: Neutral mass, Precursor m/z, Formula, Compound (e.g., 78.0464, 79.0542, C6H6, Benzene; 94.0413, 95.0491, C6H6O, Phenol). In MZmine, run the Custom Database Search with m/z tolerance = 10 mDa and RT tolerance = 0.0 (if no standards are available), mapping the CSV columns to the required fields.
